name: Winston Woodco
note: https://github.com/hakank/hakank/blob/master/minizinc/cutting_stock_winston.mzn (Winston, 'Operations Research', p. 570): 17-ft boards cut into 3-, 5- and 9-ft pieces, demand 25, 20 and 15, with the six cutting combinations the source lists.

name: AMPL cut with all maximal patterns
note: https://github.com/ampl/ampl.github.io/blob/master/docs/source/ampl/books/ampl/examples/EXAMPLES/EXAMPLES2/cut.dat (AMPL book cutting stock: 110-wide rolls; widths 20, 45, 50, 55, 75; orders 48, 35, 24, 10, 8). The book generates patterns by column generation, so the pattern list here is derived, not published: all 11 maximal patterns (no further piece fits), in lexicographically decreasing order of counts.

name: generated 4 widths 7 patterns
note: generated: roll width 30, widths 7, 9, 12, 16; after Python random.seed(11), 7 patterns drawn with random.sample from all non-empty patterns that fit (itertools.product order), then orders random.randint(3, 15) per width. Patterns are not maximal, so some waste more than needed.

name: hand-chosen overlapping patterns
note: generated: chosen by hand. Roll width 12, widths 3, 4, 5, orders 7, 5, 3, five patterns. The single-width patterns alone need 6 rolls; the optimum of 5 needs the mixed patterns (1-1-1 and 2-1-0).
